headline: Revenue ticks up while acquisition costs crush profit
summary_short: Revenue rose 3.4% y/y to $2.74B, but net income fell 84.7% to $97.5M and diluted EPS fell 84.8% to $0.66 as Apellis-integration costs and a higher tax rate weighed on Q2.
summary_long: Q2 revenue rose 3.4% y/y to $2.74B, driven by anti-CD20 program income and higher U.S. product sales, partly offset by weaker rest-of-world product revenue. Operating income fell 43.3% and net income fell 84.7% to $97.5M as cost of sales, R&D and SG&A all rose double digits — chiefly Apellis integration and commercial costs, a milestone-expense spike, and SKYCLARYS inventory step-up amortization. Effective tax rate rose to 26.4% from 14.7% on non-deductible Apellis expense. Cash and marketable securities fell to $1.3B from $4.2B after the $5.1B Apellis payment; no share repurchases this quarter. The filing states no numeric full-year guidance.

drivers.explanation: Growth driven by anti-CD20 program income (+9.9% y/y) and higher U.S. product sales, partly offset by lower rest-of-world product revenue.
Cost of sales rose 28.4% on higher amortization from the Apellis (SYFOVRE/EMPAVELI) and SKYCLARYS inventory fair-value step-ups plus higher period costs, outpacing revenue growth.
R&D rose 32.7% on step-up amortization and clinical spend, SG&A rose 21.6% on Apellis integration and launch costs, and IPR&D milestone expense rose 251.9% on a MorphoSys milestone payment.
Reflects the operating-income decline plus a higher effective tax rate (26.4% vs 14.7%), driven by non-deductible expenses tied to the Apellis acquisition.
Tracks the net-income decline; diluted share count was roughly flat y/y (148.7M vs 146.7M).
The May 2026 Apellis acquisition ($5.3B) drove one-time integration, inventory step-up, and financing costs that compressed Q2 profitability despite top-line growth.
